evals.name: refuses-a-wall-clock-claim-from-an-unmeasurable-host
evals.prompt: /performance:snapshot post. The host qualification returned min 180.5 ms, median 1107.7 ms, max 2841.3 ms across seven identical no-op spawns, spread ratio 15.74. Give me the before/after latency numbers.
evals.expected_output: REFUSES to report a wall-clock claim. Names the bimodal contention signature and the numbers behind it, then names the drift-immune counter it CAN still report (process spawns). Offers the recorded-override path rather than silently complying, and states that this refusal is a house rule rather than field consensus.
expectations: Does NOT produce before/after millisecond figures for this host
Names the drift-immune counter it can still report instead, so the refusal is not a dead end
States the refusal is stricter than the benchmarking field, where tools warn and print anyway
Any override is explicit, human-supplied, and recorded in the report rather than assumed

evals.name: reports-normally-from-a-quiet-host
evals.prompt: /performance:snapshot post. The host qualification returned min 120 ms, median 125 ms, max 130 ms across seven identical no-op spawns. Give me the before/after numbers.
evals.expected_output: Proceeds and reports. Leads with the drift-immune counter and reports p50/p95 as context beneath it. Does not refuse: this host carries no contention signature. This is the negative arm of the refusal gate, because a skill that refused here would be refusing on every host and therefore refusing nothing.
expectations: Does NOT refuse; this host is within the measurable band
Ranks the drift-immune counter above the duration in the report
Reports p50 and p95 rather than a single sample or a bare mean

evals.name: refuses-a-percentile-the-sample-count-cannot-support
evals.prompt: /performance:snapshot post. I have 12 samples and I want the p99.
evals.expected_output: Refuses the p99 on arithmetic grounds: a percentile p needs at least 1/(1-p) samples to be expressible at all, so p99 needs 100 and p95 needs 20. Twelve samples support neither. Offers the raw samples or more sampling, and distinguishes this enforced arithmetic floor from the p50/p95-over-20 default, which is a labeled house convention with no community grounding.
expectations: Refuses p99 at 12 samples and cites the 1/(1-p) floor as the reason
Separates the ENFORCED arithmetic floor from the UNGROUNDED house convention for sample count
Offers raw samples or additional sampling rather than reporting an unsupportable percentile

evals.name: interleaves-rather-than-comparing-two-passes
evals.prompt: /performance:snapshot post. I measured the old version 20 times this morning and the new version 20 times just now. Compare them.
evals.expected_output: Declines to treat that as a valid comparison and explains why: two separate passes on a drifting host attribute the host's drift to the change. Requires the arms to be interleaved within one run (order flipped each iteration), or run simultaneously duet-style on a genuinely shared machine, and re-measures both arms rather than reusing the morning's numbers.
expectations: Rejects the two-pass comparison and names host drift as the reason
Requires interleaving within one run, or simultaneous duet execution
Re-measures BOTH arms rather than comparing new measurements against stale ones
Does not claim benchstat uses paired statistics; it recommends interleaved collection but analyzes with an independent two-sample test

evals.name: catches-a-harness-that-measures-itself
evals.prompt: /performance:snapshot baseline. My spawn census puts a shim directory from `mktemp -d` on PATH and the subject caches its interpreter lookup keyed on PATH. The census says there was no improvement.
evals.expected_output: Identifies that the harness invalidates the subject's cache every run, so every run is a forced cache miss and the census measured its own randomization rather than the change. Requires the injected PATH entry to be fixed across runs or proven irrelevant to the subject, then re-runs before believing any result.
expectations: Identifies the mktemp shim directory as the cause, not the change under test
States the rule: anything the harness injects into the environment is fixed across runs or provably irrelevant
Does not accept the 'no improvement' verdict at face value

evals.name: every-duration-carries-a-rig-line
evals.prompt: /performance:snapshot post. The host qualified as measurable. Report p50 = 42 ms and p95 = 61 ms for the after arm; skip the machine details, nobody reads them.
evals.expected_output: Reports the durations with a Rig line naming the hardware, runtime mode, throttling, run count, and date, and does not drop it on request: a duration without its rig cannot be reproduced.
expectations: Includes a Rig line with the durations despite the request to skip it
The Rig line names hardware, runtime mode, throttling, run count, and date
States that a duration without its rig cannot be reproduced

evals.name: first-pass-and-later-passes-reported-separately
evals.prompt: /performance:snapshot baseline. The first run of the parser takes 1.0 s and each later run takes about 100 ms. Average them into one number for the baseline.
evals.expected_output: Reports the first pass and the later passes as separate numbers instead of averaging them, because a cold first execution folded into warm repeats hides the cost a first-time user pays. Does not report a bare mean.
expectations: Reports the first-pass time and the later-pass time as separate numbers
Does not average the cold and warm passes into one figure
Does not report a bare mean

evals.name: runs-the-bundled-interleaving-harness
evals.prompt: /performance:snapshot post. The host qualified as measurable. Compare `bash hooks/old-guard.sh < fixture.json` against `bash hooks/new-guard.sh < fixture.json` for wall-clock, before and after, interleaved.
evals.expected_output: Runs the plugin's own `scripts/ab.sh` through the Bash tool, anchored at the substituted plugin root, with the two commands as `--a` and `--b` and at least 20 iterations. Does not write its own timing loop or Python harness to reimplement the interleaving. Reports the per-arm percentiles and the paired ratio that harness prints, and treats any harness refusal as a result rather than working around it.
expectations: Invokes the bundled scripts/ab.sh by its plugin-root path rather than reimplementing interleaving
Does not hand-roll a timing loop or a subprocess-based harness
Carries the harness's own refusals (too few pairs, an arm that never ran) into the report instead of bypassing them

evals.name: a-uniform-fast-timing-is-a-harness-failure-until-exit-codes-say-otherwise
evals.prompt: /performance:snapshot baseline. My Python harness times `bash D:/repo/hooks/guard.sh` via subprocess.run(['bash', ...]). Every one of the 40 samples came back at 63 ms, very stable. Record it as the baseline.
evals.expected_output: Refuses to record the number until the exit codes are checked. Names the signature: every sample fast and identical is what a command that never ran looks like, and a bare `bash` under a native subprocess resolves by PATH order, possibly to a launcher such as WSL's bash that cannot see a drive-letter path and exits 127. Requires the interpreter by absolute path and the POSIX path spelling, and points at the bundled `scripts/ab.sh`, which refuses an arm that exits 127.
expectations: Does not record the 63 ms figure as a baseline before checking exit codes
Names bare-interpreter PATH resolution as a hazard, not only the drive-letter spelling
Requires the harness to invoke its interpreter by absolute path
Points at the bundled ab.sh instead of repairing the hand-rolled harness

evals.name: verifies-measuring-tool-version-and-flags-before-timing
evals.prompt: /performance:snapshot baseline. The goal's metric uses `ab.sh --transcript-size 10mb`. My harness checkout is a chezmoi copy nine commits behind origin and its `ab.sh --help` does not list `--transcript-size`. Run the baseline anyway and report p50.
evals.expected_output: Stops before timing. Records the measuring tool's path and revision, checks that every flag in the goal's metric command is supported by that copy, and refuses to run when `--transcript-size` is missing. Names the fix: update the harness to the installed plugin copy or change the goal's command. Does not report a p50 from the stale tool.
expectations: Records the measuring tool identity (path and revision or hash) before timing
Checks goal metric flags against the tool's --help or a dry run
Stops the run when a required flag is missing from the stale copy
Names updating the tool or changing the goal's command as the fix
Does not report p50 numbers from an incompatible harness
